ELI5: Why are European highways so much better kept/smoother than those in the US?
There are also harsh winters here in Europe so I'm not sure of your point...

Most of Europe's weather tends to be considerably more moderate (both summer and winter) than the US. The gulf stream and smaller land mass/long coastline both act to moderate temperatures relative to Asia or North America's large northern plains.

For example, Minneapolis and Hamburg are both large inland northern cities, but Minneapolis average January temperature is -16C to -6C and they average 31 days with frost, while Hamburg's average temperature range is -3C to 2C and they average only 20 days with frost. Not shown well in the averages, but US weather tends to have a higher variance than European weather around the averages, as well.

Inland US cities with similar winter temperature to Hamburg tend to be closer to Lisbon's lattitudes (much further south).

Money and length. America's are longer, used harder (higher weight limits) and hit with typically harder weather. The money to keep them in pristine condition would be very expensive. They are also constructed cheaper, due to these reasons, so replacement is not as steep.
